instructions: The night before, if your phyllo is frozen: transfer the package to the fridge to thaw.
Heat the oven to 350°F/180°C. Brush an 8-inch square baking dish with olive oil.

Trim the roots and dark green tops off the leeks. Slice the white parts into 1/2-inch rounds and swish them in a bowl of cold water to loosen any grit. Lift them out to drain. That should be about 4 cups.
Set a large skillet over medium heat and add 2 tbsp olive oil. Add the leeks, the chopped spring onions, 1/2 tsp salt and 1/4 tsp pepper.
Cook for 8 to 10 minutes, stirring now and then, until the leeks are soft and glossy. Don't let them brown.
Pour in the wine and cook for 2 minutes, until it has cooked off. Transfer everything to a large bowl and let it cool for 10 minutes.
Separate the egg. Whisk the yolk with the milk in a small bowl and keep the white for the top of the pie.
Stir the milk mixture into the cooled leeks. Crumble in the feta, grate in the Graviera and add the remaining 1/4 tsp pepper. Stir to combine.
Unroll the phyllo and cover it with a damp towel. Lay 1 sheet in the dish, letting the edges hang over, and brush it with olive oil. Repeat with 3 more sheets.
Spoon the filling into the dish and spread it level. Fold the overhanging phyllo over the filling.
Lay 1 sheet over the top, brush it with olive oil and tuck the edges down inside the dish. Repeat with 2 more sheets.
Beat the reserved egg white with 1 tsp water and brush it over the top. With a sharp knife, score the top into 8 squares, cutting about 1/4 inch deep.
Bake on the middle rack for 40 to 45 minutes, until deep golden. Let the pie rest for 10 minutes, then cut along the scored lines.

Serve warm or at room temperature. To pack it for lunch, let it cool completely and wrap it well. It keeps for 3 days in the fridge and 1 month in the freezer. Reheat slices in a 350°F oven for 15 to 20 minutes.
advance_prep_notes: thaw frozen phyllo in the fridge the night before
method_notes: My Greek Dish (the lead, 4.9 from 512 ratings) and Dimitra's Dishes agree on leeks softened in olive oil, feta, egg and layers of oiled phyllo. They differ on the extras: the lead deglazes with white wine, adds a hard yellow cheese and a milk-and-yolk binding, while Dimitra's uses a whole pound of feta with mint, dill and butter. This follows the lead, scaled down from 8 to 10 portions to 4 and baked in a small square dish. The lead's whole egg wash is split so the yolk goes in the filling and the white on top.
